text:
maya (Support): heads up — customer reported sudden quality regressions after last night's rollout. They say some responses are "stale" or mention old product names. Customer: AcmePay. Escalation opened.
josh (eng-runtime): thanks. any examples from the customer? sample request/response would help. suspecting caching layer but need evidence.
maya (Support): pasted from CS ticket:

```\nPOST /v1/chat\nAuthorization: Bearer sk-***\n{\n  "model": "rwd-chat-2",\n  "messages": [\n    {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant for AcmePay support."},\n    {"role": "user", "content": "How do I refund a payment?"}\n  ]\n}\n```

Response they received (truncated):

```\n{"id":"resp_abc","choices":[{"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"Use the old Refund API v1, endpoint /v1/refunds/create (deprecated)."}}],"meta":{"kv_cache_hit":true}}\n```

Customer insists they never saw the deprecated endpoint before — the new model should refer to `/payments/refund` (v2).

maya (Support): they attached an openapi snippet showing our earlier docs removed the v1 ref last month. So this is definitely stale output.

josh (eng-runtime): ok that "kv_cache_hit":true in the sample is telling. Can we get the API trace (request-id) and the full headers? any x-kv-* headers in the response?
eve (Customer Success): forwarded request IDs: `req-20240415-9f3a` and `req-20240415-9f3b`. Customer notes it only affects requests with a system prompt including the customer name (i.e. custom prefix). They say it started after the canary -> stable rollout at 03:12 UTC (deploy-bot shows success).
deploy-bot: release rwd-runtime@2024.4.15 deployed by josh at 2024-04-15T03:12:04Z :deploy: (canary->stable)
ryan (eng-sre): pulling traces for those req ids now. On initial glance there's a high concurrency bump and a large number of `200` responses followed by many 5xx retries from our side that correlate with autoscaler activity.

michael (eng-ml): quick hypothesis: prefix/KV caching keyed only on customer_id + prefix text, but rollout changed model variant id string (rwd-chat-2 -> rwd-chat-2-quant) and we didn't include model version in the cache key. So cached KV entries (past model) are being used with new model leading to mismatched behavior.

josh (eng-runtime): hmm that would explain stale references (model generating text consistent with older weights). Do we have an HTTP header that indicates which model provided the cached value? check `x-cache-model`/`x-kv-model`?

maya (Support): customer provided entire response headers for one request:

```\nx-request-id: req-20240415-9f3a\nx-kv-cache-hit: true\nx-kv-cache-key: prefix_usr_12345_abcd\nx-kv-cache-model: rwd-chat-2\nx-runtime-model: rwd-chat-2-quant\n```

maya (Support): note `x-kv-cache-model` != `x-runtime-model` — wow.

ryan (eng-sre): confirmed in traces. Lots of responses with `x-kv-cache-hit: true` where `x-kv-cache-model` missing version or set to previous model string. Looks like cache invalidation didn't run on the canary flip.

karen (Billing): FYI — customer retried multiple times and we saw a spike in tokens billed. If large customers retry this it could be a billing surprise. Do we have an emergency mitigation to stop billing noise?

michael (eng-ml): immediate mitigations I propose:
- invalidate KV/prefix caches for the affected model alias across regions (fast, but might be large) :warning:
- add a server-side short-circuit: if `x-kv-cache-model` != current model id, treat as MISS and bypass cached KV for that request (low-risk patch)
- rolling rollback to previous release if other regressions are happening

josh (eng-runtime): I can push a hotfix to treat model mismatch as cache miss. Minimal change in runtime: when retrieving prefix entries, compare stored cache metadata model_id to current model fingerprint. If mismatch -> delete entry and compute anew. Will route a patch in the next 20m.

eve (Customer Success): customer asked for repro steps so they can validate once we patch. I'll share exact minimal repro that triggers it:
1) system prompt includes brand name: `You are AcmePay assistant.`
2) call chat generate with model alias `rwd-chat-2` (we use alias that can point to variant)
3) repeat same prompt twice, observe second response returns content referencing deprecated endpoint

maya (Support): adding the curl they used:

```\ncurl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-customer" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"model":"rwd-chat-2","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are AcmePay assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"How do I refund a payment?"}] }'\n```

josh (eng-runtime): patch rolling out to canaries now. change log: treat model mismatch -> miss, and emit `x-kv-cache-invalidated: true` when we drop entry. Also add debug logging for cache hits with mismatched model metadata.

ryan (eng-sre): I'll coordinate regional flush and watch for CPU/GPU pressure: invalidations mean more cold starts. We should enable a temporary lower concurrency on the autoscaler to avoid overload.

karen (Billing): can we throttle customer retries or credit them if they were charged for retries caused by our bug? we should proactively offer credits if it's a billing impact.

eve (Customer Success): customer accepted temporary downtime for a short cache flush if it will fix correctness. They asked for ETA.

josh (eng-runtime): ETA ~ 30 minutes for hotfix to reach all live frontends and for us to run invalidation. I'll post back with verification steps.

michael (eng-ml): long-term fixes to avoid recurrence:
- include model_version_hash in the cache key (derived from model fingerprint + quantization flags + tokenizer version)
- on alias swap, trigger cache invalidation for that alias (or store alias->version map and lazily mark entries stale)
- add regression tests that simulate alias flip and verify no cross-variant cache hits

maya (Support): customer just replied: "thanks, please let us know when done — this caused a support surge on our side." :disappointed:

deploy-bot: rwd-runtime hotfix v2024.4.15.1 promoted to canary at 2024-04-15T03:45:20Z

josh (eng-runtime): hotfix in canary, starting gradual roll to stable. For verification, customer can run this exact sequence and include header `x-request-id`. We added the `x-kv-cache-invalidated` header on dropped entries.

maya (Support): sent quick test to customer with req id `req-20240415-9f4c`. They reported back: first call had `x-kv-cache-hit: false`, second call returned correct v2 endpoint. Customer confirms fixed.

eve (Customer Success): customer appreciates quick turnaround, asked for postmortem and assurance this won't recur. I'll collect impact numbers.

ryan (eng-sre): monitoring shows a transient increase in CPU from rebuilding KV caches but no sustained errors. autoscaler adjusted.

josh (eng-runtime): follow-ups I will file:
- PR to include model_version_hash in cache key (high priority)
- Add alias-swap hook to invalidate caches
- Improve observability: expose `x-kv-cache-model` and `x-runtime-model` consistently and log diffs to a separate telemetry stream

michael (eng-ml): add eval test case that simulates earlier weights returning deprecated docs (regression detection).

karen (Billing): I'll draft a customer credit suggestion for AcmePay and flag for revenue ops review.

maya (Support): closing loop with customer and marking incident resolved once billing credit agreed. Thanks team :thumbsup:

josh (eng-runtime): thanks everyone. I'll post the PRs and the short incident note in /postmortems once we have final numbers and root cause.
